summary: npm package used as jsDelivr CDN vector for browser redirect/adware with domain rotation
details: The package's main script is a browser-only payload that injects a full-screen iframe loading https://mfmz.gszfgt.cn/H.html?c=0gjr into any page that embeds it via the jsDelivr CDN. There are no install/preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks and no Node-side execution: `require()` throws immediately because `document` is undefined, so a developer who installs the package into a Node project is not harmed. The tarball additionally ships `update_px8my.sh`, a maintainer script that rewrites the redirect host inside px.js (regex `mfmz\.[^/\\]+`), bumps the patch version, runs `npm publish`, and purges the jsDelivr cache — an automated rotation loop consistent with adware/redirect distribution that evades takedowns by publishing new versions under fresh domains. The npm+jsDelivr channel is being used as a redirect-hosting CDN rather than as a JavaScript library; the harm surface is browser end-users of sites that embed px8my via jsDelivr, not developers who npm-install it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
